subject: Clarifying export clearance, retention windows, and deletion attestation for audit/access logs
messages:
From: Anna Li <anna.li@healthx.net>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Finvero Compliance Team <compliance@finvero.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Export/retention questions for audit & access traces

Rishi — thanks for taking this. Quick context: HealthX is doing a security review ahead of our upcoming SOC-2 re-assessment. The compliance reviewers want to understand three things for tenant-scoped audit/access logs: 1) retention windows you support for tenant-level exports (we'll need both short-term snapshots and a full archive export), 2) whether exported archives can be scoped by region and encrypted with a customer-managed key, and 3) your process/attestation for deletion once a customer requests an erase.

Specific asks: 
- Can you provide the maximum historical window available for a one-shot export?
- Do incremental exports (delta since last export) exist? If so, how are they generated and deduplicated?
- Are exported bundles signed/hashed so we can verify integrity after transfer?
- What proof do you provide that an audit log subset was deleted from Redwood systems (index/tombstone + storage wipe attestations)?

We may loop in Legal but wanted a product-level answer first. Appreciate any sample artifacts (manifest, sample playbook, or signed attestation).

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Li
Head of Information Security, HealthX

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example.com>
To: Anna Li <anna.li@healthx.net>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.example.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.example.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Export/retention questions for audit & access traces

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary and then a couple of attachments (export playbook + example manifest). I also flagged Monica and Grace to cover contractual/deletion attestation details.

Short answers up front:
- Max one-shot export window: we can produce a contiguous export of audit/access events for up to 7 years from the tenant's creation timestamp, subject to the customer's retention policy and any legal holds.
- Incremental exports: yes — we offer delta exports via our "export-stream" endpoint. Deltas are generated from the event index (sequence IDs) and include a monotonically increasing sequence number to enable idempotent replays and deduplication on the recipient side.
- Regional scoping & CMK: exports can be scoped to region (us/eu/apac) and delivered as encrypted archives. For Private customers we support wrapping the archive with a customer-managed key (KMS/HSM integration). For Hosted customers we offer envelope encryption with a customer-provided KMS key via our KMS connector.
- Integrity & signing: exported bundles include a SHA-256 manifest and an optional PKCS#7 detached signature. Bundle manifests list filenames, sequence ranges, and a content-hash per file.
- Deletion attestation: we provide a deletion report that includes (a) tombstone record ids (sequence ranges) removed, (b) storage object deletion receipts (object ids and delete timestamps), and (c) a signed attestation (by our compliance team) for Reserved/Private customers. For Hosted customers we provide the same report but the attestation is provided as a standard deletion certificate (no HSM signature unless under an enterprise plan).

Notes and caveats: 
- Exports that include encrypted payloads still may contain metadata (object/sequence IDs). If there are export requests spanning cross-border constraints, we recommend scoping the export to the requested residency region to avoid transit of identifiable metadata.
- One-shot 7-year exports for very large tenants are delivered as chunked archives (multipart export) with an index for reassembly. Delivery SLA depends on size; we provide an ETA estimate in the export request response.

I've attached: redwood-audit-export-options-2025.pdf (playbook) and a small sample manifest (export-schedule-sample.csv). Let us know if you want the PKCS#7 demonstration signed by our compliance lead.

Next step: Monica — can you outline the attestation scope we can commit to in a standard enterprise T&Cs vs. a bespoke contract?

Best,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Product Compliance — Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: redwood-audit-export-options-2025.pdf (9 pages), export-schedule-sample.csv (3 rows)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.example.com>
To: Anna Li <anna.li@healthx.net>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.example.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2025 13:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Export/retention questions for audit & access traces

Hi Anna — copied in Grace who handles legal attestations. A couple of points from the contracts side: 

- Standard enterprise commitment: we provide a deletion certificate (signed PDF) stating the records deleted and the deletion timestamps, plus storage object delete receipts. This is included in our Dedicated and Private plans; for Hosted customers we offer the same outputs but sign-off is via an automated deletion certificate (no HSM signature).
- For customers who require an HSM-backed attestation (e.g., public sector or regulated healthcare), we can add an addendum: attestation signed with a customer-key-wrapped certificate and an independent timestamping service. That requires ~6–8 weeks lead time for onboarding and an additional compliance review.
- Pricing note: long-window one-shot exports (multi-TB) and HSM attestations are billable. We'll include a cost estimate once we see the export size.

Grace — can you prepare a redlined clause sample for HSM-backed deletion attestations? Anna — if you confirm that HealthX needs HSM-level evidence, let us know and we'll start the scoping questionnaire.

Thanks,
Monica
Monica Patel
Sr. Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference

Thanks — that helps a lot. HealthX will likely ask for the HSM-backed attestation because of our regulatory scope in Europe and an upcoming legal hold scenario. Please initiate the scoping questionnaire and share the cost estimate for a 4 TB one-shot export with HSM attestation. Also: could you include a sample signed manifest (PKCS#7) with the playbook so our infra team can validate the verification process?

I'll loop in Legal once I have the redlined clause. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best regards,
Anna
